questions.prompt: Which objective lens must be in place when you first put a slide on the stage?
questions.explanation: Before securing a slide: stage at its lowest position and the 4X objective clicked into place.

why.C: 40X is used later in the focusing sequence.

questions.prompt: The coarse adjustment knob may be used with which objective lens?
questions.explanation: Use both coarse and fine knobs on the 4X lens; fine focus is enough for all other objectives. NEVER use coarse with 40X or 100X.

why.A: Never use the coarse knob on 40X or 100X.
why.C: These are exactly the lenses where coarse focus is forbidden.
why.D: Coarse focus at 100X can smash the lens into the slide.

questions.prompt: Our microscopes are 'parfocal.' What does that mean?

options.text: All objective lenses have the same magnification power
When one objective is in focus, the others are too, needing only fine adjustment
The microscope can focus on two separate specimens
The focus knobs adjust both of the eyepieces at once

questions.explanation: Parfocal: when one objective lens is in the correct focus plane, so are the others — switching lenses keeps the specimen in focus with only fine adjustments.

why.A: Each objective has a different magnification (4X, 10X, 40X, 100X).
why.C: Parfocal refers to the focus plane staying the same.
why.D: Parfocal concerns objective lenses, not eyepieces.

questions.prompt: What are the four objective lenses on the brightfield microscope?

options.text: 4X low power, 10X scanning, 40X oil, 100X high power
4X scanning, 10X low power, 40X high power, 100X oil immersion
4X scanning, 10X high power, 40X oil, 100X dry lens

questions.explanation: 4X scanning, 10X low power, 40X high power, 100X oil immersion.

why.A: The names are mixed up — 4X is scanning and 100X is oil immersion.
why.B: There is no 20X lens; scanning is 4X.
why.D: 10X is low power, 40X is high power, 100X uses oil.

questions.prompt: With a 10X ocular lens, what is the total magnification when using the 40X objective?

why.B: Total magnification multiplies the lenses, it doesn't add them.

questions.prompt: With a 10X ocular lens, what is the total magnification under oil immersion (100X)?
questions.explanation: Total magnification = 10 × 100 = 1,000X — the magnification used to view bacteria.

why.A: Multiply the lenses, don't add them.

questions.explanation: Viewing bacteria requires the 100X oil immersion lens and immersion oil.

why.A: Bacteria require the 100X oil immersion lens.
why.C: Bacteria are far too small at 10X.

questions.prompt: Where is the drop of immersion oil placed?

options.text: On the 40X lens before switching to 100X
On the slide above the specimen, with the nosepiece between 40X and 100X
On the condenser below the stage of the microscope
On the ocular lens before looking through it

questions.explanation: Rotate the nosepiece halfway between 40X and 100X, place 1 small drop of oil on the slide, then rotate the 100X lens into the oil.

why.A: NEVER put oil on the 40X lens.
why.C: Oil goes on the slide above the specimen.
why.D: Oil goes between the slide and the 100X objective.

questions.prompt: You're at 100X with oil and can't find the specimen after a little fine focusing. What should you do?

options.text: Follow the clean-up procedure and restart the focusing process
Go back to the 40X lens to find it
Use the coarse knob to move the stage up
Add more oil and keep turning the fine focus

questions.explanation: Don't go back to 40X. Follow the clean-up procedure and restart the focusing process.

why.B: NEVER go back to 40X after using immersion oil.
why.D: The protocol says clean up and restart.

questions.prompt: What is used to clean oil off the slide, the 100X lens and the stage?
questions.explanation: Clean-up: 4X back in place, lower the stage, remove the slide, then use vinegar on fresh Kimwipes for the slide, the 100X lens and the stage.

why.A: Bleach isn't used on microscope lenses.
why.D: The protocol uses vinegar on Kimwipes.

questions.prompt: When you are done with oil immersion, what is the first clean-up step?

options.text: Rotate the 4X scanning lens into place
Wipe the 100X lens with a Kimwipe
Remove the slide from the stage

questions.explanation: Clean-up order: 4X into place → lower the stage completely with coarse knob → remove the slide → clean slide, 100X lens and stage with vinegar.

why.B: Lens cleaning comes after moving to 4X, lowering the stage and removing the slide.
why.C: Unplugging happens at the very end.
why.D: First rotate to 4X, then lower the stage.

questions.prompt: Which part do you adjust to change the amount of light passing through the condenser?
questions.explanation: Adjusting the iris diaphragm changes the light passing through the condenser and improves resolution.

why.A: The fine knob focuses the specimen.

questions.prompt: This purple-stained sample shows chains of rods. What kind of microscope image is it?

options.text: Brightfield — a stained specimen on a bright background
Darkfield — specimen glowing on a dark background

questions.explanation: Brightfield: light through the field of view appears bright, and stained specimens provide contrast.

why.C: SEM images are 3-D grayscale or false-color surfaces.
why.D: Fluorescent specimens glow against a dark background.

questions.prompt: In the Oil Immersion skills assessment, what must you accurately describe once you are focused?

options.text: The specimen's Gram reaction and species name
The number of colonies on the slide
The total magnification at each lens

questions.explanation: Independently focus to oil immersion on a prepared bacterial slide and accurately describe its morphology, without a protocol.

why.B: The assessment is focusing to oil immersion and describing morphology.
why.C: Colonies are counted on plates, not slides.
why.D: You report the morphology of the bacteria.

questions.prompt: Which statement about using the brightfield microscope is FALSE?

options.text: Use the coarse knob to bring the 100X lens into focus
Lower the stage fully before placing a slide
Center the specimen over the light beam
Never put oil on the 40X lens

questions.explanation: NEVER use the coarse adjustment knob with the 40X or 100X lenses — it can smash the lens into the slide.

why.B: True — the stage starts at its lowest position.
why.C: True — adjust the stage so the specimen is over the beam.
why.E: True — oil is only for the 100X lens.
